title: Credential handoff where the model never sees secrets: executor-side fill_secret and email OTP via integration-corev2
summary: Add a fill_secret action carrying an opaque vault:// reference that Quarry resolves only at execution time through the integration-corev2 token broker, fills in an isolated world after re-checking origin and field type, and then blocks page observation of the filled value; add an IC mail.otp.read action so email one-time codes are delivered by the executor after user approval. Requires a sensitive BrowserBroker grant, capture-time redaction (F-t2-021), trusted input (F-t2-015), takeover (F-t2-013) and a Model Plane elicitation/approval card.
whyItMatters: Both browser references keep secrets out of the model (Codex: isolated-world fill, OTP and QR, SRC; Aside: origin-bound vault refs, SRC). Verevon has no secret references; fill_secret exists only as a plan (reconciled plan section 19.1, DOC). The present fallback, human takeover login into a scoped profile, works for attended runs but blocks unattended agents and routines.

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Agent calls request({origin, fields[{label, selector, autocomplete}], submit}). The runtime validates origin and selector uniqueness/visibility; the UI shows a secure form or vault picker; values travel executor -> CDP isolated world -> input.value plus input events; the agent receives only {status}. The document is marked credential-delivered and AX/DOM/screenshot reads of that loader id are denied until navigation. || Merged items add: Model calls browserAuth.request(otpHandle) on a tab. Runtime proceeds only if: origin is https; frame origin equals top origin; exactly one required non-password input; no options/QR; credential-observation gate on; conversation id bound; otherwise status 'unavailable'. It then raises a user elicitation (kind browser_email_otp, requires user input, not auto-approvable by a guardian) saying the model cannot see the code and the user may type it instead. On approval the host (not the model runtime) fetches the code from the mail connector over a local broker socket (versioned credential binding) and types it through a native input path; the model receives only a status. Note Codex restricts this to non-password fields.

verevonToday.gap: No secret store with opaque references reachable from Quarry; integration-corev2 vault and Quarry profiles never meet at runtime; planned only in docs (SRC/DOC).

approach: ADR on secret custody across planes first (IC owns secrets; Quarry resolves at execution; Model Plane sees only the reference). Then IC operations, Quarry fill_secret with origin and field preconditions plus redaction, Model Plane elicitation event and frontend approval card. || Source detail: [R-t2-09-04] Ingestion Plane: fill_secret action plus an observation gate and redaction of receipts and live frames (blank or blur credential fields). Frontend: secure credential form outside the live frame. Secret store with opaque references scoped to user/org lives in the owning plane (Control Plane per the comparator; check integration-corev2 credential handling first) and is read through its API only. Model Plane: planner sees only ref ids and status. || [R-t2-10-01] Ingestion Plane owns execution; Model Plane owns the approval. (1) Quarry contracts (quarry-core contracts.rs AgentAction plus the Go pkg/quarrycontracts mirror): add FillSecretRef { snapshot_id, generation, ref_id, secret_ref } and FillOtpRef; secret_ref is an opaque handle such as secret://connection/<id>/mail-otp, never a value. (2) browser-broker: add a fill_secret entry to allowedSensitiveActions and issue it through CreateScopedSensitiveApproval as a single-use child of the run grant, bound to one origin, one frame and one secret_ref with a short TTL, only after a user approval event routed by Model Plane/Conversation. (3) integration-corev2: add a dedicated mail.otp.read action (sender/age/pattern filters, returns the code only, write-attested user context, audited through the existing outbox) so Quarry never holds a mailbox OAuth token; do not just add quarry to INTEGRATION_TOKEN_LEASE_CONSUMERS. Add the Quarry-to-IC row to the cross-plane service-token manifest. (4) Quarry executor: precondition checks (https, frame origin == top origin == grant origin, exactly one visible required non-password input for OTP, no QR/options), fill via CDP Input.insertText, mask the field in screenshots/DOM snapshots, receipts carry a boolean only, nothing persisted under ZDR. (5) Frontend: elicitation card naming origin and connection, stating the model cannot see the value, and offering "I will type it myself". Ship OTP first; passwords/vault secrets only after the redaction and prompt-injection defences are proven.
dependencies: Secret store with opaque references (existence unverified)

Quarry value-level redaction pipeline for observations, receipts and artifacts
New IC mail.otp.read action for Gmail and Outlook connections
Model Plane approval/elicitation event and frontend approval card
planeOwner: Ingestion Plane (Quarry executor + integration-corev2 vault) + Model Plane (elicitation)
risks: Live frames and screenshots can leak typed secrets; never log values; secrets scoped per user/org, never per Space; ZDR must hold (no persistence of frames that show credentials). || Secret exfiltration through a phishing page, injected iframe or weak origin matching; OTP requested by a page the agent was lured to; accidental logging in receipts, screenshots or artifacts; ZDR violations if a value persists; prompt-injection that tricks the model into proposing fill_secret on the wrong origin (so approval must show origin and connection and be single-use). Quarry has no prompt-injection defences yet per the comparator.

verevon.constraints: Ingestion Plane owns execution and secret resolution, and the model only ever sees opaque references (Model proposes, Quarry executes); secrets are scoped to user or org and never widened by Space access. ZDR: no persistence of values or frames showing credentials, yet non-ZDR receipts today store typed text verbatim, so redaction (F-t2-021) must precede any fill action. IC Vault is token-at-rest encryption, not a user-secret store, so a secret-custody ADR is required before password references; IC internal auth is one shared API key (server.go:170-173), so Quarry to IC needs a distinct identity or manifest row, and the OTP action must stay off any Model-callable tool surface and return only the code. Production BrowserBroker grant issuance is unbuilt (shared prerequisite with F-t2-001 and F-t2-013).
verevon.approachAdjustment: Ship OTP first: add a fill_otp variant beside upload_ref and download_ref in the existing sensitive-approval path (single-use child grant bound to run grant, frame and origin), an executor-only IC mail.otp.read action, and reuse the Login risk gate and orchestration approvals for the approval card instead of a new elicitation channel. Defer password and vault-secret references until the secret-custody ADR, F-t2-021 redaction and F-t2-015 trusted input are in place. Do not add quarry to INTEGRATION_TOKEN_LEASE_CONSUMERS.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged for the OTP-first slice; the full password and secret-store scope would be XL because of the ADR, redaction and grant-issuance prerequisites.
verevon.verdictReason: Confirmed absent in code, but the item should be reworded to OTP-first on top of the existing sensitive-approval and login-gate machinery, with the vault/secret-store half explicitly deferred behind an ADR and its prerequisites.

reference.corrections: 1) Re-attribute: Codex browserAuth (secure sign-in handoff, isolated-world native delivery, credential observation gate, email OTP) is wired to the CDP client in the hosted 'gaas-browser-environment' (Codex Cloud Browser) via a broker socket; the shipped desktop in-app browser (iab client) does not advertise the browserAuth capability and the broker socket env is forwarded only in Dev builds.
